findings.title: Broken Zod schema for minimum token response

Calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema returns a fixed string like `"ZodString"`, not a property name pattern. This does not create a schema that accepts any string key with a number value (as the comment suggests); instead it creates a single hardcoded key with an arbitrary name. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, every call to `safeParse` will validate against this broken schema, likely rejecting all valid sync responses (or accepting them with wrong types). The intent was probably `z.record(z.string(), z.number()).optional()` or similar. All sync-path token refreshes will fail validation and throw "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned".

Even in the non-sync path, any schema that doesn't require `refresh_token` (e.g., the Salesforce schema) will have its existing refresh_token overwritten by this literal string before the spread in the caller, unless the caller explicitly re-overwrites it (as Salesforce does, but Google Calendar and Office365 do not).
